«far from being an exhibitionist visionary, always kept secret also this gift of the divine goodness (visions and others); only to paper did she confide the manifold representations. In her responsibility as foundress she showed concern about those spiritual directors who gave too much credit to the sisters who said they had visions, with the risk of favoring a false spirituality and of making such souls fall into the deceits of Satan»318.

3. Participation in the Passion of Jesus

118. — Among the interior and exterior extraordinary phenomena of Mother Rosa Gattorno, her participation in the Passion of the Redeemer emerges, in the form of stigmata, crowning with thorns, pain of the wounds in the feet, hands and side. These externally invisible forms were the expression of her profound participation in the motives of Jesus' passion and in the love with which he lived it.

The signs of participation in the passion, indeed, are granted by God only to lead the person to a greater likeness to the suffering Christ; at the same time God also intends to present to the Church a message, so that her attention to the mystery of redemption may be stronger and she may feel urged to a greater love of the cross and to the desire of atonement for her own sins.

In this perspective Pius XI spoke

«of St. Francis of Assisi who by his stigmata was a particular example of Christ crucified; with his stigmata he came almost to propose to humanity the meditation and imitation of Jesus Christ crucified»319.

The Servant of God, with this extraordinary participation in the passion of Jesus, enters fully into the passion-centered spiritual vein that has characterized Catholic spirituality in a particular way from the Middle Ages to our own day.

Mother Gattorno is neither the first nor the last to have received from God these particular and visible signs of the passion of Jesus. In Italy we can recall, besides St. Francis of Assisi, various Servants of God who received different forms of bodily participation in the passion of the Lord, such as: St. Veronica Giuliani, St. Clare of Montefalco, and, contemporary with Mother Gattorno, St. Gemma Galgani.

Of the latter, during the iter of the Cause, there was much discussion on the truth of the extraordinary mystical phenomena which, for a long period of her life, made her share in the various moments of the passion of Jesus: crowning with thorns, scourging, bloody sweat, stigmata in the feet, hands and side. The scholars, after long discussions, recognized the truth of the testimonies, the supernaturality of the phenomena found, Gemma's psychic balance. They were not, however, spoken of in the decree on the heroicity of virtues320.

119. — In this our century there have been no lack of other Servants of God who have had in abundance the same gifts as Mother Gattorno, such as: Sr. Elena Aiello, Fr. Pio of Pietrelcina, Teresa Fusco, to remain in Italy and among those whose Cause of canonization is being conducted. This means that the path of the Servant of God is extraordinary but at the same time not unique. This helps to see her process of identification with Christ crucified in a more positive context within Catholic spirituality. Rightly, therefore, Fr. Iriarte finds the explanation of the extraordinary mystical phenomena of the Servant of God in her firmly passion-centered spirituality:

«Christ Crucified was the center of Rosa Gattorno's spirituality and, therefore, configuration to him, in spirit and in body, could not but be her supreme yearning. Her preferred, daily contemplation was that of the Passion. As in the other true stigmatics, this contemplation and that conforming love disposed her to receive the gift of the bodily projection of the Redeemer's wounds, which were already fixed in her spirit»321. Only that, in keeping with her desire not to cause admiration through extraordinary graces, she obtained from the Lord that everything remain hidden: she had, indeed, the pain of the wounds, but not the external signs»322

The same Fr. Iriarte concludes:

«Scholars of mystical phenomena in general, and in particular of stigmatization, give no importance today to the miraculous character or otherwise of the bodily manifestations, but to the cause that produces them. True stigmata are those somatic localizations or projections that originate in the infused contemplation of Christ's sufferings in the Passion, even if, as is known of some canonized saints, a volitional inclination to arrive at that loving identification with the Crucified preceded. What counts is the sincerity of the subject who experiences it»323.

4. Psychic balance of the Servant of God

120. — The psychic health of a person also counts, and much, in the whole of that person's mystical phenomena.

Mother Rosa was a perfectly healthy and balanced woman, as is deduced from the most carefully weighed and exhaustive opinion which Most Rev. Fr. Paolino Zavarella, «Expert in re medica», at the request of our Congregation for the Causes of Saints, gave in 1982, «on the state of normality, or otherwise, of the Servant of God, Rosa Gattorno, with express indication of its nature and of its degree of relation to impairment of personality».

Fr. Zavarella, after studying the problem in depth in a long writing which in the present Positio occupies the not small extent of 35 pages (from p. 859 to p. 894), formulates these conclusions:

«From the medical point of view in general and, particularly, from the point of view of the question I must answer, I must admit that the objective finding of the exercise of all the virtues, at a high level and prolonged in time, constitutes a further solid argument to show that Rosa Gattorno always enjoyed great psychic balance.

In this connection ample and due importance must be attributed to what has been set forth, at a time and in circumstances beyond suspicion, by the doctors who treated the Servant of God, particularly in the last years of her earthly life, and to what highly qualified persons have reported on her psychic state; the study has made it possible to ascertain that:

1. The doctor who had the Servant of God in his care during the last 12 years of her life affirms, and decisively, the perfect psychic balance of the patient.

2. The notary Tommaso Monti, who drew up Gattorno's holographic will, personally ascertained, in repeated conversations, her normality.

3. The confessor, Fr. Vincenzo da Alatri, uses particularly elevated words in describing the uprightness and uncommon perfection of the Servant of God.

4. Her whole complex existence, the way she lived married life, the circumstances of the foundation and the surprising development of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, show by the proof of facts that Gattorno was not only normal from the psychic point of view, but was a person rich in high qualities.

5. The comparative examination between the work Travagli e conforti and all the other writings of Gattorno shows a perfect self-mastery, a more than notable psychic balance, great capacities for accomplishment and (especially in the vast correspondence) a continual exercise of charity in understanding, directing, comforting others.

Consequently, to the doubt proposed concerning the normality of the Servant of God, I reply that Rosa Gattorno was a person certainly normal from the psychic point of view»324.

121. — Most Rev. Fr. Lázaro Iriarte adds further:

«Normality does not mean an ordinary level; Rosa Gattorno was not a common woman, her spiritual stature was not confined within the current banks.

p. 137

Already in life she had to undergo verifications of the authenticity of her spirit. Indeed, among the priests with whom she tried in vain to find adequate guidance, there were not lacking some distrustful ones who wished to see clearly in that case which fell outside ordinary ascetical frameworks»325.

At this point Fr. Iriarte gives the word to Mother Rosa herself, who thus writes in her Memoirs, on 21 July 1887:

«By order of my direction, I had to submit to an examination, regarding my spirit, by a priest of holy life. After having examined well — which he did in a moment —, he said and wrote thus: that one must not look in me at the creature, but only at the work of the Creator. I remained as if he had known well that it was and is always the most skillful Artificer who works in me and through me and that, looking at the creature, there is nothing else than misery and nothingness»326.

Conclusion

122. — And here is the conclusion of Fr. Iriarte, which we gladly make our own:

«Without heeding the interpretation, inspired by humility, of the Servant of God, we can say that the verdict of the good religious remains still valid for an objective judgment on the case of Rosa Gattorno. We could, for example, call into doubt the supernatural nature of many of her visions, of her prophetic predictions, of her intuition of the interiority of persons; we might not accept that torturing of her body in inhuman form [...]; but one thing is beyond doubt: the work of the Creator. This action of the Supreme Good, as she (Mother Rosa) likes to call him, is evident both in the mystical experience of the Servant of God and in the direction, as foundress, of that which she invariably designates by the name of ‘Work of the Lord’»327.

One thing is certain in the whole of the mystical phenomena that so abound in Mother Rosa's earthly story, and it is the evident positive incidence of these phenomena on the spiritual life, of union with God and of prolific apostolate of the Servant of God.

In confirmation of this may we be allowed to cite these words of Fr. Fiocchi, from the biography he wrote on Mother Rosa Gattorno:

«The charisms of the grace of union brought to Mother Rosa not only the sweetnesses that prelude heaven, but also the precious adornment of the most solid virtues, which befit the true Servant of God and make her worthy to follow the Lamb in the mystical nuptials: and this, we believe, is the best seal of the truth of those gifts. They, the mystical gifts, are a purely gratuitous bestowal of divine goodness and are not properly required for holiness: often, however, they accompany it and are given as a reward for singular surges of generosity or as means of particular missions in the

Church of God. But they cannot be found in the spiritual desire of dissipated or wicked souls, because they presuppose the love of God and are its highest exercise: and here is apt what is read in Scripture: ‘In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia’ (Wis 1:4). If in souls stripped of virtue something unusual sometimes flashes in communications with God, one must proceed with great caution in giving it credence, for easily there will be the deception of the angel of darkness, who loves to transform himself into an angel of light»328.
